clue.text: Destroyed by devils and a radicalised …

indicators.note: radicalised means changed fundamentally, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Something was wrecked by demons and an extremist, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radicalised' reads as describing a person, but it is the anagram signal for DEVILS AND A. The trailing dots link the surface to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that has been wantonly smashed up or defaced has been destroyed in the deliberate, malicious way the word implies.

clue.text: … Soviet leader, restoring Ivan the Terrible, last letters of literati lost

indicators.note: restoring means storing again in a new arrangement, so the pooled letters are reordered
lost tells us the letters of the word literati are taken out of the pool

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader brings back the memory of a tsar while educated people disappear, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of IVAN THE TERRIBLE plus Z, with the letters of LITERATI removed, leave VNHERBE + Z to be rearranged. 'letters of' just points at the word literati.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonid Brezhnev led the USSR as General Secretary of the Communist Party from 1964 until 1982.

clue.text: Small change to charity creating sacred music

parts.note: P and S, penny and shilling, are the abbreviations of small coins
alms are gifts given in charity to the poor

explanation.surface: Dropping a few coins in a collecting box somehow produces church music.
explanation.walkthrough: P (penny) and S (shilling) are old British coin abbreviations, so loose coins give PS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Psalms are the sacred songs of the Bible, still sung or chanted in church services.

clue.text: Slothful doctor gets home help

indicators.note: the doctor gets something into him, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
an ai is a three-toed sloth, and slothful here is read as full of sloth

explanation.surface: A lazy GP takes on someone to help around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slothful' is not an adjective here: it is read as full of sloth, the AI being a sloth; MD takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic servant who cleans and tidies is a home help, the classic household helper.

clue.text: Jesus' words of comfort for the poor in spirit etc: "Go and renegotiate dues!"

definitions.text: Jesus' words of comfort for the poor in spirit etc

parts.note: beat it is slang for go away

indicators.note: to renegotiate is to rework terms, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Jesus's comforting words are oddly paired with a brusque order to leave and rethink one's subscription.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes in the Sermon on the Mount begin 'Blessed are the poor in spirit', blessings that comfort the lowly.

clue.text: Heroically, ecstatically proletarian: no hothead, no alternative

indicators.note: a proletarian is non-U, not upper class, so the letter U is dropped
the second no again means without, removing the next piece
no here means without, so the following piece is removed

parts.note: euphorically means in an ecstatic way
the head of hot is its first letter, H
or offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A rousing description of a passionate working-class hero, stripped of rashness and choices.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from EUPHORICALLY; 'proletarian' (non-U, a British class label for not upper class) removes U, 'no hothead' removes H and 'no alternative' removes OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done epically is done on the grand scale of an epic poem, which is to say heroically.

clue.text: Looking up to quote work of lyrical quality

indicators.note: in a down entry looking up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone checks a quotation from a piece that has a lyrical feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that is poetic has the lyrical, expressive quality of verse.

clue.text: Soviet leader on former Axis: "It's hot"

parts.note: S is the initial standing for Soviet, as in USSR
ex means former
Y names the y-axis of a graph

explanation.surface: A Russian leader standing beside a wartime ally claims to be attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soviet leader' and 'Axis' summon twentieth-century history, but here they give S and the y-axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot in slang means sexually attractive, so something described as hot is alluring.

clue.text: Industry for high flyers rapidly embracing lust

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: apace means quickly
Eros is the Greek god of desire, standing for lust

explanation.surface: A business for jet-setters is moving fast while wrapped up in desire.
explanation.definitionFit: The aerospace industry builds aircraft and spacecraft, the things that fly highest.

clue.text: Call to reduce phobias (as justice ought to be) on Tyneside

indicators.note: to reduce is to cut something down by removing part
justice ought to be without bias, so the letters of bias are taken away

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A plea to cure Geordies of their irrational fears, with an aside about fair justice.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone is to telephone them, so the verb to ring up fits.

clue.text: Hypnotised with spots of light instead of softly snoring

indicators.note: one thing in place of another means a swap of letters

parts.note: dappled means marked with patches of light
pp is pianissimo, very softly in music
zz is the cartoon sound of snoring

explanation.surface: Someone in a trance sees flecks of light and has stopped snoring gently.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dazzled is to be overwhelmed and spellbound, as if mesmerised.

clue.text: Without a word of thanks, left in London?

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the City is the financial district of London

explanation.surface: Someone departs London without even saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed tacitly is understood silently, never put into speech.

clue.text: In bonds, hopes

definitions.meaning: to yearn or wish is a verb meaning hopes

explanation.surface: Someone imprisoned and still hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a plural noun for long-dated gilts and a verb meaning yearns.

clue.text: Fortitude beside explosive device found at highest level on vessel

definitions.text: found at highest level on vessel

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage
a cap is a small explosive charge, as in a toy cap gun

explanation.surface: Courage next to a bomb is discovered at the top of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a bottle-like container.
explanation.definitionFit: A closure that sits on the top of a bottle is literally at the highest point of the container.

clue.text: Scene of overindulgence and wicked bare greed by name?

indicators.note: wicked means twisted, perverse, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setting of gluttony where plain greed is named for what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's outdoor drinking area is where people overindulge in alcohol.

clue.text: They guide the coach's team after taking number one with pride

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
I is the Roman numeral one
a pride is a group of lions

explanation.surface: A sports coach's assistants take charge after the side wins with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' and 'team' suggest sport; it is a horse-drawn coach and its team of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Postilions ride the leading horses of a carriage team, steering the coach.

clue.text: They include envy, with idle sadness in some versions

definitions.text: They include envy, with idle sadness in some versions

indicators.note: versions means variant forms, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A list of moral failings that sometimes included sadness, alongside envy.
explanation.walkthrough: Medieval lists of sins sometimes named sadness (tristitia), so the whole clue defines as well as builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy and sloth (idleness) are among the classic list of capital vices in Christian teaching.

clue.text: One freshly converted to make war, say

definitions.text: One freshly converted to make war, say

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are reordered
say signals that the following word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to fight is to make war

explanation.surface: A recent recruit to a cause who is eager for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a novice, originally a new convert to a religion.

clue.text: One unfortunate formerly embraced, then cut off

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a poor sod is an unfortunate person
late means formerly, as in the late president

explanation.surface: A luckless person once hugged then cut dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off means left separate or alone, without contact.

clue.text: Dog sled is worked in shifts

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A husky's sled is used in rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something is to move it from its place, as dislodging does.

clue.text: Some tabloid on showing temperance

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
dry means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A popular paper running an item on sobriety.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or several, as in sundry items, close to some.

clue.text: Eastern root of many outsiders ornamenting life in capitals

indicators.note: capitals here are the capital, opening letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: An oriental root garnishing the lives of many foreigners in big cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooli is a long white radish, a root vegetable from South and East Asia.

clue.text: Note: wrath is an illusion

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
rage means wrath

explanation.surface: A remark that anger is just an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen in a desert.

clue.text: He employs cowboys with spurs, no nonsense, wiser at last

indicators.note: no here means without, so a piece is dropped

parts.note: spurs are side shoots or branches of a tree
BS is slang for nonsense

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter

explanation.surface: A Western boss with spurs who stands for no nonsense and grows wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurs' evokes cowboy boots, but means branches of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher owns a cattle ranch and hires cowhands to work it.

clue.text: Losing some faith finally in prudence, causing split

indicators.note: losing means taking away, so letters are removed

parts.note: thrift is prudence with money
some of the word faith: its closing pair of letters, T and H

explanation.surface: Loss of religious belief in a careful person leads to a rupture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' says which part of faith is meant: its final two letters, removed from THRIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a break or schism, a split in a relationship or rock.

clue.text: Dish sent back, Boatman saying: "No meat"

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are turned around

parts.note: the setter Boatman refers to himself as I
nay means no
a rib is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A diner returns a dish, the setter declaring that it should have no meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Biryani is a spiced rice dish from South Asia.

clue.text: Raised Soviet leader to become first

indicators.note: first says this piece goes at the front
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Red is a common term for a Soviet communist

explanation.surface: A communist chief was promoted to the top position.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means reared or brought up, as children or livestock are raised.

clue.text: 22 down's confused, where victory lies in virtue

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the answer to 22 down with an s added

explanation.surface: A split in a group breeds confusion, while morality wins out.
explanation.walkthrough: V, the abbreviation for victory, is the first letter of virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: The position of V within the word virtue is the opening one, at the very start.

clue.text: Always strong and stable but inside loveless, therefore concerning

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the pieces go into the other one

parts.note: even, as in even so, can mean but or yet

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so loveless drops an O

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
re means concerning

explanation.surface: A political slogan of strength and stability, with a logical argument about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong and stable' echoes a 2017 slogan of Theresa May, then UK prime minister; 'loveless' uses love = O, the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes something perennially fresh and lasting, always vigorous.
